d: Using integers as bitmasks to represent subsets or states in DP, usually when N is very small (N < 20).

p: When N is extremely small (N < 20), we can use an integer bitmask to represent which items have been selected. This converts subsets into array indices, enabling incredibly fast DP caching.
1. Mask 000 means nothing visited. Mask 111 means items 0, 1, 2 visited.
2. To check if bit `i` is set: `mask & (1 << i)`.
4. Pass the mask into your memoized recursive function.

# Example: Check if all N items are visited
ALL_VISITED = (1 << N) - 1
if mask == ALL_VISITED:
  return True
Time: O(N * 2^N). Space: O(2^N) for the DP cache.

Items: 0, 1, 2
Mask 000: None selected
Mask 011 (3): Items 0 and 1 selected
Mask 101 (5): Items 0 and 2 selected
Mask 111 (7): All selected
